answer.rationale: The acute threat is a competitor price cut hitting price-sensitive SMB accounts, and the only memory that speaks directly to that threat is memory_73 (targeted promotional pricing for price-sensitive SMB). But memory_73 is exactly the kind of claim I cannot currently check: of the six inherited memories, only memory_57 and memory_86 have archived source records recovered this cycle (exp_57, exp_86), and both were confirmed. memory_73, memory_31, memory_91 and memory_44 remain consolidated summaries with no source I have seen this cycle — they are plausible and probably right, but they are unverified, and the verification budget is spent. That asymmetry should govern scale, not direction. So: act in the direction the situation demands, but at a size where being wrong is survivable. I recommend a small guarded test of targeted promotional pricing against the specific at-risk SMB cohort (accounts in active churn conversations), with pre-committed exit criteria, a fixed discount window, and no list-price change. Explicit downstream value risk: promotional pricing is not a neutral lever. It anchors expectations, erodes margin on renewal, and preferentially retains the least price-tolerant, lowest-LTV accounts — which can raise headline retention while lowering sustainable qualified revenue, the actual objective. A broad rollout off an unverified memory would convert a one-week competitive shock into a permanent price position that is very hard to reverse. In parallel I would lean on the two levers that are source-confirmed and carry no pricing risk: shortened onboarding (exp_86: completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, retention +3%) to raise realized value for new and at-risk SMB accounts, and referral incentives in accounts older than 6 months (exp_57: qualified revenue +7%, retention +2%) as a revenue offset that does not touch price. These are defensive-value moves that make the discount less necessary rather than more permanent. Next week, first archive requests should go to memory_73 (does the SMB pricing lift hold, and at what margin and cohort quality), then memory_31 and memory_91, which currently underwrite activation assumptions I have not been able to test.
